simple.meaning: גִּיחַ (gîyach) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to gush forth (as water), generally to issue.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 6 times across Judges, Job, Psalms, Ezekiel, Micah, beginning at Judges 20:33. Its contexts include family, family line, kingship, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גִּיחַ (H1518).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: גִּיחַ (gîyach) / H1518 is traced through Judges 20:33, Job 38:8, Job 40:23, Psalms 22:10 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H1518. giach [ גּוּחַ גִּיחַ, ] verb burst forth (compare Nö ZMG 1883, 538 ; Late Hebrew id. , Aramaic id. , and ; Ethiopic break forth , of light, etc.) — Qal Imperfect יָגִיחַ Job 40:23 , masculine singular וַתָּ֫גַח Ezek 32:2 ; Imperative feminine singular גֹּ֫חִי Micah 4:10 ; Infinitive suffix (בְּ)גִיחו Job 38:8 ; Participle suffix גֹּחִ֫י Psa 22:10 (but compare below); — 1 intransitive burst forth , of dashing river (a very Jordan) Job 40:23 ; of sea figurative as babe from womb 38:8 , compare 2 transitive a. draw forth from womb (subject ׳י ) Psa 22:10 (where read גָּחִ֫י participle from גּוּחַ , or regard גֹּחִי as metaplastic, as if from ג֗֗֗חח ? see De & Che critical note ) compare 71:6 ; also b. thrust forth, bring forth , rather ' break forth (with that which is to be born),' figurative of travail, applied to Jerusalem in distress Micah 4:10 (compare Sta § 599 b Kö i. 505 ); burst forth with rivers (figurative of Pharaoh under image of תַּנִּים ) Ezek 32:2 , but for בנהרותיך ( rivers ) read probably בִּנְחִרוֺתֶיךָ Job 41:12 ( nostrils ), i.e. snort with thy nostrils, so Ew Co; on figurative then compare 41:11-13 .
